statement.p: Suppose that f(x) is a function with f(95) = 61 and f'(95) = 2. Estimate f(97).

static.solution: f(95) = 61 and f'(95) = 2 tell us that at x = 95, the value of the function is 61 and the function is increasing at a rate of 2 units for a unit increase in x. Since we increase x by 2 units in going from 95 to 97, the value of the function goes up by approximately 2 \cdot 2 = 4 units, so f(97) \approx 61 + 2 \cdot 2 = 61 + 4 = 65.
